stories.title: Development of (polyvinyl alcohol/O-carboxymethyl chitosan/PbO) nanocomposites for efficient gamma radiation protection
stories.description: A polymeric blend based on polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) / carboxymethyl chitosan was developed for gamma radiation shielding applications. The nanocomposite films were fabricated using a simple solution casting method, where the readily available nanosized lead oxide PbO particles were dispersed within a polymer matrix composed of PVA, polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP), and citric acid. The dispersion process was assisted by sonication before crosslinking, ensuring uniform distribution of oxide particles throughout the films. The physicochemical properties of the synthesized nanocomposites were systematically characterized using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX), X-ray diffraction (XRD), ultraviolet–visible spectroscopy (UV–Vis spectroscopy), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), water vapor permeability (WVP), soil burial degradation, and total soluble matter (water absorption) measurements. Gamma shielding performance was evaluated through the determination of linear and mass attenuation coefficients (μ and μ/ρ) at photon energies ranging from 59.53 to 1332 keV, using a NaI (Tl) scintillation detector with standard gamma-ray sources (Am-241, Ba-133, Eu-152, Cs-137, and Co-60). Additional shielding parameters, including half-value layer (HVL), tenth-value layer (TVL), and mean free path (MFP), were calculated. The experimental linear and mass attenuation coefficients for the blank sample, which closely matched the theoretical predictions from XCOM, verified the produced films’ outstanding gamma radiation shielding capabilities. PbO nanoparticles were incorporated into the chitosan matrix to produce a uniform and compact film structure. HVL, TVL, and MFP, among other computed shielding factors, showed how well the nanocomposites attenuated gamma photons throughout a broad energy range. Furthermore, the structural stability, uniform shape, and environmental degradability of the composites were validated by physicochemical studies. These findings demonstrate that carboxymethyl chitosan/PbO nanocomposite films are attractive options for long-term radiation protection, as they combine efficient radiation-shielding capabilities with other desirable properties. While carboxymethyl chitosan/PbO nanocomposite films show promising radiation shielding efficiency, their long-term stability remains a concern, as partial material degradation may affect their sustained performance.

stories.title: Marriage-divorce dynamics in Azerbaijan, 2014-2023: a time-series study
stories.description: Marriage stability and union formation are central to household stability and long-term demographic sustainability. Azerbaijan has experienced a clear inversion in nuptiality patterns, with declining marriage rates and rising divorce rates, yet high-frequency evidence on these dynamics remains limited. This study provides the first decade-long, high-resolution econometric assessment of Azerbaijan’s marriage-divorce dynamics using integrated structural-break and ARDL modeling. The time-series strategy applies Seasonal-Trend decomposition using Loess (STL) followed by ARIMA (p,d,q) modeling to capture dynamic persistence after seasonal adjustment and to identify stochastic patterns. Structural breaks are formally tested using Chow breakpoint tests at the known intervention date (2020 Q2) and Bai–Perron multiple-break procedures. The structural determinant model is specified as an ARDL(2,2) framework linking divorce rates to unemployment, inflation/Consumer Price Index (CPI), and the institutional e-registry reform variable, with cointegration assessed through bounds testing and long-run multipliers reported explicitly. Statistical inference relies on heteroskedasticity-robust (HC1) standard errors and Wild-Bootstrap confidence intervals (999 replications), and robustness is verified using alternative trend filters and exclusion of pandemic years. In 2014–2023, marriage rates declined by –0.34 (95% CI: –0.47, –0.22) per 1000 population annually, while divorce rates increased by +0.08 (+0.04, +0.11). A statistically significant structural break in 2020 Q2 (τ = –4.27, p = 0.01) confirmed pandemic disruption. The ARDL results indicate that a one-percentage-point rise in unemployment increases divorce by 0.43 per 1000 in the long run, while a five-percentage-point inflation shock raises divorce by 0.12 per 1000. The digital marriage-registration reform reduced divorce by 0.14 per 1000, suggesting early institutional mitigation effects. Macroeconomic variables jointly explain 61% of divorce variation (adjusted R² = 0.61). Children born in unregistered unions declined by 38.7% over the study period. Forecasts indicate marriages may recover to 5.9 per 1000 by 2026 if unemployment remains below 5%, but could stagnate under renewed labor-market shocks.

stories.title: A Curated Flow Imaging Microscopy Dataset of Subvisible Protein Aggregates from Stressed Monoclonal Antibodies
stories.description: Subvisible particles (SvPs) are critical quality attributes of injectable monoclonal antibody (mAb) therapeutics, as they are associated with reduced product stability and increased immunogenic risk. Flow imaging microscopy (FIM) has emerged as a key analytical technique for SvP characterization, providing rich image-based information that enables morphological analysis beyond traditional particle counting methods. Despite growing interest in applying machine learning to FIM data, publicly available datasets of subvisible protein particles remain largely unavailable due to commercial and proprietary constraints. To address this gap, we present mAb-SVP-20K, a curated dataset containing 20,000 FIM images of subvisible protein aggregates acquired from eight commercially derived monoclonal antibodies subjected to controlled heat and mechanical stress conditions. All images are provided as raw, unprocessed instrument outputs, accompanied by detailed methodological documentation and technical validation. With this dataset, our goal is to support reproducible research, enable rigorous benchmarking of computational and machine learning methods, and facilitate data-driven investigations of stress-induced particle formation in monoclonal antibody products.
